description:
Goal (2026-09-15): make every user-facing string in the app translatable and ship Japanese (ja) as the first non-English UI language, on both the phone companion UI and the G2 glasses UI.

Scope: UI language only. Spoken-language work (language ID, per-language model routing, code-switching, summary language choice; plan.md §15 "Multi-language support") and live translation are separate and out of scope here. The existing `Settings.language` (recording language) stays as is and is independent of the new UI language.

Current state (survey 2026-09-15):
- Phone UI: Solid 2.0 rc in apps/even-hub/src/ui (App, History, Recording, Live, People, SpeakerSheet, Settings (648 lines), Diagnostics, Evaluation). All strings are hardcoded English JSX; no i18n library.
- Glasses UI: apps/even-hub/src/glasses.ts hardcodes loading/ready lines, menu labels ("Start recording", "Save audio: on", "Add marker", "Stop and summarize"), hints ("Tap to start. Double tap to exit."). Menu labels are capped by G2_MENU_LABEL_MAX_BYTES and bodies by TEXT_LIMIT via truncateUtf8; Japanese is 3 bytes/char in UTF-8, so English-sized budgets hold ~1/3 as many characters.
- English also originates outside the app: domain selection.ts disabled reasons and option labels, identity.ts match reasons ("Unknown", "Possibly Alice", "Speaker 2"), SERVICE_NAMES, LANGUAGES names, pipeline export.ts markdown header and default "Recording" title, and Error messages surfaced through errorMessage().
- Dates use toLocaleString with the default locale (App.tsx, lib.tsx "Today, …", export.ts).
- apps/even-hub/app.json: "supported_languages": ["en"]; the network permission desc is English.

Approach:
- New @irl/i18n package with no Solid dependency (usable from glasses.ts, pipeline export, and the UI): en catalog as `as const` source of truth, ja typed against the same shape so a missing key fails typecheck; parameterized messages as functions; Intl.PluralRules / Intl.DateTimeFormat / Intl.NumberFormat bound to the resolved locale; fallback to en. A thin Solid wrapper exposes the locale as a signal so a language switch re-renders immediately (unlike recording settings, which apply to the next recording).
- Packages return codes/structured reasons, not English sentences; the UI edge localizes them.
- New setting `uiLanguage: "system" | "en" | "ja"` (default "system", resolved from navigator.languages, or the Even Hub host locale if the SDK exposes one) with a settings migration.
- Evaluation view stays English (developer tool); Diagnostics is localized.

```mermaid
graph LR
  S[1 spike: G2 CJK glyphs + host locale] --> G[6 glasses strings]
  S --> M[9 app.json + store metadata]
  F[2 i18n package + uiLanguage setting] --> P[3 phone UI extraction]
  F --> D[4 domain/pipeline messages as codes]
  F --> T[5 locale-aware dates, numbers]
  F --> G
  F --> C[8 Japanese typography CSS]
  P --> J[7 Japanese catalog]
  D --> J
  G --> J
  T --> J
  J --> V[10 on-device verification]
  C --> V
  M --> V
```
title: UI localization (i18n): translatable phone and glasses UI, Japanese first
